title: The Sarbat Khalsa
hookLine: a gathering of the whole panth, rare today and much discussed

cards: Who gets a say? A family planning a wedding finds out fast. So does a band choosing its name, or a club picking a captain.
Somebody always asks: did everyone get asked, or just the loud ones? Behind the Takhts, and the five Sikhs who decide for the community, stands a bigger idea.
What if, for the gravest questions, the whole panth came together in one place, in the Guru's presence, and decided as one? Sikhs have a name for that gathering.
It's old, it's rare today, and Sikhs argue about it with real feeling.

teach.b: The name is Sarbat Khalsa. Sarbat means all, the whole of something. Sikhs hear the same word each time the Ardas, the common prayer, closes by asking for the good of all, sarbat da bhala.
So Sarbat Khalsa is the whole Khalsa: all of us together. Now the history, told carefully.

teach.h: MEETING AT AMRITSAR, BEFORE THE GURU.
teach.b: Sikh histories describe a time after the Tenth Guru when Sikh bands were scattered and often hunted, and their leaders would meet at Amritsar at festival times; you met those meetings earlier on this path.
Tradition says they gathered before the Guru Granth Sahib, talked through what faced them, and made a gurmatta, a resolution taken in the Guru's presence.

Once made, it was meant to bind everyone, even those who had argued against it. That's the idea at its best: no single ruler, no single family, but the gathered panth and the Guru together. Then the hard part.
Who calls a Sarbat Khalsa today? Who counts as the whole, when Sikhs live in many countries and belong to many organizations?
When gatherings have been called under this name in recent times, Sikhs have disagreed, sometimes sharply, about whether they truly spoke for all. Some hold that the Akal Takht should call it.
Some want new ways for distant Sikhs to take part. Some think the old form fits the old days best. This path won't settle it.
Under the argument sits the hope inside the word: that the Guru's community can still decide as one.

how: A Sarbat Khalsa is a gathering of the Sikh community before the Guru Granth Sahib to pass a gurmatta, a binding resolution; gatherings under this name are rare today and their authority is debated among Sikhs.

practice: Bring to mind the last time a group you belong to made a big choice, and look for the one who wasn't in the room, or who was there and said nothing. Don't fix anything.
Just picture the whole group sitting in a circle, that person included, every voice given room.
